predecessors.name: Alemanni
predecessors.text: the Alemanni's land (Alsace, the Rhine and Main country, Swabia) passing to the Cliopatria row Kingdom of Alamannia

successors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
successors.text: the duchy of Alamannia, ruled by Frankish dukes after the Cannstatt council and directly by Pepin the Short from 748

ledger.x: 462: the Kingdom of Alamannia appears between Strasbourg and Augsburg.
496: Clovis beats the Alemanni at Tolbiac and the Franks take the northern half.
536: the Franks under Theudebert I subjugate the Alemanni again and the kingdom becomes a nominal Frankish duchy.
746: Carloman's blood court at Cannstatt ends the duchy.

wars.name: Battle of Tolbiac
wars.outcome: Frankish victory: 'The Franks were successful at Tolbiac and established their dominance over the Alamanni'; the northern half went to the Franks, the southern half to Theoderic's protection.

wars.name: Frankish subjugation of Alamannia
wars.outcome: The Alemanni were 'again subjugated by the Franks under Theudebert I in 536'; Alamannia became a nominal dukedom within Francia.

wars.name: Frankish campaigns against the duchy of Alamannia
wars.outcome: The Arnulfing mayors of the palace reduced Alamannia to a Frankish province: Pepin of Herstal against Lantfrid 709-712, Charles Martel 722 and 730, Pepin the Short and Carloman 743, the Cannstatt blood court 746.

certainty.note: A tribal kingdom 'between Strasbourg and Augsburg' with no recorded frontier; the western and northern limits are approximate.

The Lech to the east and Lake Constance at the centre are the only features the Alamannia page gives; Alsace, Raetia and the Swiss Plateau are ill-defined, and the Cliopatria data has no shape for 500-723, so the keyframe is a reading.
